title: Deterministic artifact hashing and release-broker for staged profile promotion
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a deterministic artifact hashing and release-broker subsystem that automates model build/sign/promulgate (staged profile promotion) for CI/CD onboarding. The goal is a reproducible model artifact pipeline that produces a canonical hash used for pinning in serving configs and a broker service that coordinates TTL-based staged promotions (canary -> stable) while enforcing signature and provenance checks.
background: Currently model onboarding relies on ad-hoc hashes and manual promotion steps. This causes accidental pin drift, unverifiable rollouts, and slow manual gating for performance profile publication. We need reproducible artifact hashes plus an automated promotion broker that centralizes policy (canary %, time windows, automated rollback on perf regression) and emits verifiable release metadata consumed by serving and the console.
acceptance_criteria: CI produces a deterministic artifact hash for a given model build input (same inputs => same hash) using canonical serialization and pinned buildenv
Artifacts are signed with cosign and recorded in a transparency log (Rekor) and verify during promotion
Release-broker can accept a signed artifact and perform staged promotions: canary -> primary within configured time windows and audiences
Serving layer accepts pin references by artifact-hash (sha256) and rejects unsigned or mismatched provenance
Performance profile JSONs are published as part of the artifact bundle and are immutably associated with the artifact hash
End-to-end e2e test covering build -> sign -> verify -> canary promotion -> stable promotion exists and runs in pipeline (ci/onboard/e2e-release-flow)
Documentation and runbook for key rotation, emergency rollback, and manual override stored in Confluence
implementation_notes: Use deterministic build container: toolchain pinned (gcc/python versions), sort protobuf/manifest fields, normalize floats to canonical rounding before hashing
Artifact bundle layout: /model.tar.gz, /profiles/perf.json, /manifest.json (includes input hashes, builder-id, deterministic-checksum)
Signing: cosign for container/artifact, push signature to Rekor; store verification materials in artifact metadata
Broker API: POST /releases with signed-artifact-ref, policy payload (canary_pct, canary_duration, fallback_policy), returns release_id and timeline
Broker will publish release metadata into serving catalog and console; serving pulls only when signature+provenance validated
CI jobs to add: ci/onboard/build-deterministic, ci/onboard/sign-publish, ci/onboard/verify-promote, ci/onboard/e2e-release-flow
Telemetry: emit events for build_hash, sign_time, promote_step, rollback_reason to analytics pipeline and console dashboard
Graceful rollback: broker monitors perf regression signals (from quality-monitoring pipeline) and can revert pins automatically and notify stakeholders
test_plan: Unit tests for canonical serialization library (round-trip reproducibility)
Integration tests: build same source twice in CI -> expect identical hash
Signature verification test that rejects tampered artifacts
Simulated canary: inject 1% traffic, validate latency and correctness metrics, then promote
Chaos test: broker process restart and idempotency (reconcile to desired state)
End-to-end CI job (ci/onboard/e2e-release-flow) runs on PR to master and on nightly
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature-flagged broker accepts internal test models only; docs and dev runbook published (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): enable for selected platform-team models; run canary promotions automatically (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): open to all model onboard flows, integrate with onboarding UI and console release dashboard (1 week)
Emergency path: manual override endpoint for SRE with RBAC; immediate unpin and fallback to previous artifact hash
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Non-deterministic build inputs (timestamps, random seeds) => Mitigation: canonicalize outputs, strip timestamps, seed deterministic builders
Risk: Key compromise for signing => Mitigation: KMS-backed signing with HSM integration, enforce key rotation cadence and maintain Rekor transparency
Risk: Broker misconfig promotes bad profile => Mitigation: require perf smoke tests before auto-promotion and configurable canary % with minimum duration
Risk: Increased CI time => Mitigation: cache intermediate build artifacts and reuse existing reproducible-builder images
